translations.text: David said to him, “What is the news? Tell me.” He said, “The people fled from the battle, and many of the people fell and died. Saul and Jonathan also died.”
David said to him, “Your blood is on your own head, because your own mouth testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the Lord’s anointed.’”
Stand still, Israel, over the wounded on your hills, on your heights! How the mighty have fallen!
Do not tell it in Gath, and do not announce this news in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice and the daughters of the uncircumcised celebrate.
Now let your hands be strong, and be valiant men, for your lord Saul has died, and the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.
They rose and went across, twelve in number from the young men of Benjamin belonging to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from David’s young men.
Abner and his men traveled eastward all that night, crossed the Jordan, went through the whole stretch of land, and came to the camp.
David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, “Give me my wife Michal, whom I married in exchange for a hundred foreskins of the foreigners.”
David said to Joab and to all the people with him, “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” King David walked behind the bier.
Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, went and entered Ish-bosheth’s house during the heat of the day, while he was sleeping on his bed at midday.
David took more wives and concubines from Jerusalem after leaving Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
And it happened, when David was settled in his house and the Lord had given him rest from all his enemies around him,
And I was not humbled at all before you, Lord, my Lord, and you spoke at length concerning the house of your servant. Is this the law of humanity, Lord, my Lord?
Now, my Lord, establish forever the word you spoke concerning your servant and his house, and do as you have said.
David placed garrisons in Syria opposite Damascus, and the Syrians became David’s servants, bringing tribute. The Lord delivered David wherever he went.
David said, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul, so that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
He seized David’s servants, shaved off their beards, cut their [?] through the middle down to the edge, and sent them away.
Uriah said, “All is well.” David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” Uriah left the king’s house, and a gift from the king followed him.

Who struck Abimelech, the son of Jerubbaal, the son of Ner? Did not a woman throw a piece of a millstone down on him from the top of the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you approach the wall? Then you shall say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.’
When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband Uriah had died, she mourned for her husband.
For you did this in secret, but I will do this thing in the sight of all Israel and before this sun.

Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Now, my sister, keep silent, for he is your brother. Do not take it into your mind to speak of this matter.” Tamar lived as a widow in the house of her brother Absalom.
The king rose, tore his clothes, and fell to the ground. All his servants stood around him with their clothes torn.
Your maidservant had two sons. The two fought with each other in the field, and there was no one to intervene between them. One struck the other brother and killed him.
Three sons and one daughter were born to Absalom. Her name was Tamar, and she was very beautiful in appearance. She became the wife of Rehoboam son of Solomon and bore him Abijah.
Whenever a man approached to bow down before him, he would stretch out his hand, draw him close, and kiss him.
The king and his entire household went out on foot, and the king left ten women from among his concubines to look after the house.
Their two sons are there with them: Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar. Send me through them everything you hear.
In those former days, the advice Ahithophel gave was as though someone had sought a word from God. Such was all Ahithophel’s advice, both to David and to Absalom.
I will come upon him at night, when he is weary and his hands have lost their strength. I will terrify him, and the troops who are with him will flee. I will kill only the king.
I will bring all the troops back to you, as a bride returns to her husband. You need seek the life of only one man, and all the troops will be at peace.
After they had gone, the men came up out of the well and went and told King David. They said to David, “Get up and cross the water, for Ahithophel has planned this and that against you.”
The king gave orders to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, “Spare my young man Absalom.” All the troops heard the king giving orders to all the commanders concerning Absalom.
The troops of Israel were defeated there by David’s servants. There was a great slaughter that day, and twenty thousand men fell.
Joab said, “For that very reason, I will go on ahead of you.” Joab took three darts in his hand and thrust them into Absalom’s heart while he was still alive in the oak tree.

But while Absalom was still alive, he erected a monument for himself and set up the monuments in Jabin, in the Valley of the Kings, for he said that he had no son to preserve the memory of his name. He named the monument after himself, and it has been called Absalom’s Monument to this day.

You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. Today you have shown that you think nothing of your commanders or your servants. Today I know for certain that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, that would please you.

All the people throughout all the tribes of Israel were troubled and said, “King David rescued us from all our enemies and saved us from the hands of the Philistines. But now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom because of Absalom.”
“Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now why do you remain silent about bringing the king back?”
He turned the hearts of all Judah as though they were one man. They sent word to the king, saying, “Return, you and all your servants.”
Barzillai said to the king, “How many days of my life remain, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?”
Then all the men of Israel came to the king and said to him, “Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan?”

There a lawless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite, grew bold. He blew a horn and said, “We have no share in David and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Israel, let every man go to his own dwelling!”

The woman went to all the people and spoke to the whole city with her wisdom, urging them to cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri. They cut it off and threw it to Joab. He blew the horn, and they dispersed from that city, each man to his own home. Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
Let seven men from among his sons be given to us, and we will hang them up before the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, the Lord’s chosen one. The king said, “I will give them to you.”
He went up and sat upon the cherubim and flew, and he appeared upon the wings of the winds.
For you are my lamp, Lord, and you, Lord, will light up my darkness.
To make my feet like a deer’s; and he sets me upon the heights.
He said, “Far be it from me, Lord, to do this! Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” And he would not drink it. These things the three commanders did.
Helez the Paltite; Ira son of Ikkesh, the Tekoite.
They came to Mapsar of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they came from the southern side to Judah and to Beersheba.
They went around the whole land and arrived in Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

David said to Gad, “I am in great danger on every side. But now let me fall into the hands of the Lord, for his mercies are very great, and let me not fall into human hands.” David chose the plague for himself, and it was the time of the wheat harvest.
The Lord sent a plague upon Israel from morning until midday, and the destruction began among the people. Seventy thousand men died among the people, from Dan to Beersheba.
